Q2.e: s3: key idx 3 only. Line 3 ('그래서 뭐라고 하셨어요?') is also subject-less and its honorific fits BOTH 사장님 and 팀장님, so it is arguably the more genuinely ambiguous line, but pickLine gives not-match (empty message). The keyed line 4 ('...보자고 했어요') is itself unnatural Korean: a speaker reporting what a superior said would say 하셨어요, so the item teaches 'a missing honorific makes the subject ambiguous', which a native speaker would read as the speaker being 태호 or a rude omission. s4: w1 rejects '사장님 오실까요? ... 곧 오신대요' (실까요/오신 not listed, false rejection) and a chat with a full-width ？ or no ? fails w2; w1 accepts a chat with no honorific at all if it contains 안녕하세요 (세요), e.g. 'A: 안녕하세요? 오늘 뭐 해요? B: 안녕하세요, 공부해요.' (false acceptance).

themes: Write-step regex checks are the weakest part: shared polite-ending regex [가-힣]요(?![가-힣])|니다|니까 accepts casual -니까 sentences; per-step keyword lists accept wrong content (k-01 w2 matches the refused day, k-06 w1 matches 절반 in 'no refund', k-09 sofa 'today', k-03 plain agreement, k-05 negated promise) and reject valid wording (살게요, 반액, 조용히, 병원에 가야 해서, 오실까요).

Cue-solvable multiple-choice: k-07 s1 and k-11 s1 (the one 해요체 option), k-03 s1 (only option with both times), k-12 s1/s2/s3 (single honorific cue), k-02 and k-08 s2 (longest/only sensible option). Hints in k-07/k-11 name the cue.
Diagnostic value uneven: reveal-type steps (k-05, k-10) have no per-option reveals; k-07/k-11 wrong-set reveals mostly absent or 'this is suitable'.
Topic overlap: speech-level tasks k-02, k-07, k-11; soft-refusal/pleasantry k-01 and k-08; heavy pragmatics knowledge is taught afterwards rather than inferred.
Language defect k-12 s3: keyed 'ambiguous' line ('...보자고 했어요' about a superior) is unnatural Korean; other lines checked are natural. k-09 model answer '종이이면' unnatural (use '종이 박스면').
No unsafe/biased content found; minor male default for 부장님 in k-12; emoji and table accessibility are described in text. k-04 beginner reading load exceeds stated prerequisites.
